abstract: The Philippines is a common ground to natural calamities like typhoons, floods, volcanic eruptions and earthquakes. With Twitter as one of the most used social media platform in the Philippines, a total of 39,867 preprocessed tweets were obtained given a time frame starting from November 1, 2013 to January 31, 2014. Sentiment analysis determines the underlying emotion given a series of words. The main purpose of this study is to identify the sentiments expressed in the tweets sent by the Filipino people before, during, and after Typhoon Yolanda using two variations of Recurrent Neural Networks; standard and bidirectional. The best generated models after training with various hyperparameters achieved a high accuracy of 81.79% for fine-grained classification using standard RNN and 87.69% for binary classification using bidirectional RNN. Findings revealed that 51.1% of the tweets sent were positive expressing support, love, and words of courage to the victims; 19.8% were negative stating sadness and despair for the loss of lives and hate for corrupt officials; while the other 29% were neutral tweets from local news stations, announcements of relief operations, donation drives, and observations by citizens.

bibliographic.title: Sentiment Analysis of Typhoon Related Tweets using Standard and Bidirectional Recurrent Neural Networks

content.problem: Despite Filipinos producing vast amounts of tweets during natural disasters, very little research has tapped this data to understand the emotions Filipinos express on Twitter during calamities such as Typhoon Yolanda.
content.proposed_solution: The authors collect and preprocess Typhoon Yolanda related Filipino tweets, manually annotate a balanced sample of 3,900 tweets as positive, negative, or neutral, and train standard and bidirectional recurrent neural networks with Word2Vec features and varied hyperparameters to classify sentiment before, during, and after the typhoon.
content.algorithm_or_model: Standard and bidirectional Recurrent Neural Networks
dataset_testbed: Typhoon Yolanda related Filipino tweets collected from Twitter (39,867 preprocessed tweets; 3,900 manually annotated)

metrics.name: accuracy
metrics.condition: Fine-grained (3-class) classification using standard RNN with batch size 64, learning rate 1.80E-03, dropout 0.5, and truncated BPTT

metrics.name: accuracy
metrics.condition: Binary classification using bidirectional RNN with batch size 64, learning rate 1.80E-03, no dropout, and full BPTT

metrics.name: F1 Score
metrics.condition: Fine-grained (3-class) classification using standard RNN with batch size 64, learning rate 1.80E-03, dropout 0.5, and truncated BPTT

metrics.name: F1 Score
metrics.condition: Binary classification using bidirectional RNN with batch size 64, learning rate 1.80E-03, no dropout, and full BPTT

content.claim: Both standard and bidirectional RNNs proved effective for typhoon-related tweet sentiment analysis, scoring above 80% on all evaluation metrics with best accuracies of 81.79% for fine-grained and 87.69% for binary classification, and applying the trained model to the full dataset revealed that 51.1% of tweets were positive, 19.8% negative, and 29% neutral.
author_stated_limitations: The trained models misclassify a noticeable share of tweets as false negatives, causing 14% and 12% inaccuracy for the standard and bidirectional models on binary classification and 12% and 11.9% on fine-grained classification.

evidence.problem_quote: Considering this vast amount of data, it is relatively untapped since very few studies have so far been conducted to analyze the tweets of Filipinos in terms of emotions expressed through tweets.
evidence.proposed_solution_quote: The main purpose of this study is to identify the sentiments expressed in the tweets sent by the Filipino people before, during, and after Typhoon Yolanda using two variations of Recurrent Neural Networks; standard and bidirectional.
evidence.claim_quote: The best generated models after training with various hyperparameters achieved a high accuracy of 81.79% for fine-grained classification using standard RNN and 87.69% for binary classification using bidirectional RNN.
author_stated_limitation_quotes: In the error analysis of binary classification, the cause of the 14% and 12% inaccuracy for standard and bidirectional models respectively is based on false negative misclassifications.
